note: Views Contextual Range Filter turns a Views contextual filter (argument) into a range filter driven by the URL using -- (or :) as the from--to separator (inclusive). It provides argument plugins numeric_range/string_range/date_range, a numeric_range argument validator, and a php_default argument-default plugin. Filters are converted on /admin/config/content/contextual-range-filter (route contextual_range_filter.settings, perm 'administer contextual range filters'); doing so records the machine name (table:field) in contextual_range_filter.settings under numeric_field_names / string_field_names / date_field_names AND rewrites the View's argument plugin_id to the *_range variant. Its own recorded state is that settings config object, which the medium/hard cases are grounded in (Views-entity building is avoided because an unrelated broken contrib module fatals the Views plugin managers on this shared site). Permissions: 'administer contextual range filters' and the restricted 'use php code for default contextual filter'.

evals.prompt: Using the Views Contextual Range Filter module, how do I write a URL argument that filters a View to items with a price between 100 and 199.99, and how do I make an open-ended 'from 100 upwards' range?
evals.expected_output: Append the range as a contextual argument using -- (or :) as the separator: /yourview/100--199.99 for the closed range, /yourview/100-- for 100 and up, and /yourview/--199.99 for up to 199.99. All ranges are inclusive.

evals.prompt: Which Views argument (contextual filter) plugins does the Views Contextual Range Filter module provide for numeric, alphabetic and date ranges?
evals.expected_output: It provides three argument handler plugins: numeric_range (extends NumericArgument), string_range (extends StringArgument, case-insensitive) and date_range (extends Date). It also adds a numeric_range argument validator and a php_default argument-default plugin.

evals.prompt: There is no checkbox in the Views UI to make a contextual filter a range filter. How do I convert an existing contextual filter into a contextual range filter, and where does the module record that choice?
evals.expected_output: Add the plain contextual filter in Views first, then go to /admin/config/content/contextual-range-filter (route contextual_range_filter.settings) and tick it. That records the machine name in contextual_range_filter.settings (numeric_field_names / string_field_names / date_field_names) and rewrites the View's argument plugin_id to the *_range variant.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, one field has been converted into a NUMERIC contextual range filter with the Views Contextual Range Filter module. Inspect the live contextual_range_filter configuration and give the field that was converted.
evals.expected_output: It is node__field_crf_probe:field_crf_probe_value (i.e. field_crf_probe): contextual_range_filter.settings numeric_field_names lists it (drush cget contextual_range_filter.settings numeric_field_names).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, one field is configured as a STRING (alphabetic) contextual range filter with the Views Contextual Range Filter module. Inspect the live configuration and name that field.
evals.expected_output: It is the node title (node__field_data:title): contextual_range_filter.settings string_field_names lists it (drush cget contextual_range_filter.settings string_field_names).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, register the field with machine name node__field_crf_task:field_crf_task_value as a NUMERIC contextual range filter using the Views Contextual Range Filter module's settings. Apply the change to the live configuration.
evals.expected_output: Add 'node__field_crf_task:field_crf_task_value' to the numeric_field_names list in contextual_range_filter.settings and save (this is what ticking the filter on /admin/config/content/contextual-range-filter records).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, the field node__field_crf_toggle:field_crf_toggle_value is currently registered as a numeric contextual range filter. Convert it back to a plain contextual filter by removing it from the Views Contextual Range Filter settings. Apply the change to the live configuration.
evals.expected_output: Remove 'node__field_crf_toggle:field_crf_toggle_value' from numeric_field_names in contextual_range_filter.settings and save (unticking it on the settings page).
